subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should Windows exec support inline PowerShell `$` expansion payloads through an explicit one-shot approval path, or should OpenClaw document those payloads as unsupported and require script-file/direct-command workarounds?
rationale: Current main rejects these tokens in approval analysis, and changing that behavior touches command execution safety, allowlist reuse, and Windows command fidelity; automation cannot choose that product/security contract for maintainers.

options.title: Support One-Shot Expansion Approval
options.body: Adopt the open PR direction once it has redacted real Windows/Gateway proof that expansion-bearing commands reach explicit one-shot approval without auto-review or hanging.

options.title: Document Unsupported Inline Payloads
options.body: Close the implementation path and update exec docs/tool guidance to make script-file or non-inline PowerShell usage the supported Windows workaround.

options.title: Wait For Live Repro Matrix
options.body: Keep this issue in needs-info until a reporter or maintainer provides current-main Windows proof for plain, quoted, escaped, double-dollar, and `cmd /c` cases.

recommendation.title: Support One-Shot Expansion Approval
recommendation.body: Adopt the open PR direction once it has redacted real Windows/Gateway proof that expansion-bearing commands reach explicit one-shot approval without auto-review or hanging.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available routing owner from history because this decision spans the current shell-selection contract and the current main checkout owner signal.
